newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens sees static Asian after-tax profit.
newsitem.headline: Siemens sees static Asian after-tax profit.

text.p: German industrial group Siemens Ag said on Sunday it expected after-tax profit in its Asian businesses to be about 300 million marks in the year to the end of September 1997, unchanged from a year ago.
Guenter Wilhelm, head of Siemens' Asia-Pacific activities, said results in the region would be dampened by a loss in its Indian unit.
"I think we have a loss (in India). The financial year is not over, I don't know how much it will be yet," he told journalists at a news conference.
Wilhelm said he expected orders in Asia in 1996/97 to increase to 10 billion marks, up from nine billion last year.
Emerging markets in the region were driving growth in sales of advanced communications and electronics technologies and large infrastructure projects, Wilhelm said.
"Today Asia Pacific is in the midst of an unprecedented boom, showing the world's most dynamic growth," he said.
However, he cautioned that "it is hard to make money there", because of intense price competition.
Earlier, a colleague of his on the management board, Juergen Radomski, said Siemens planned to increase sales in Asia by 20 percent a year and expected volumes of over 25 billion marks there by 2001.
Siemens is due to release its nine-month results here on Monday.
